name: Shopify
look: Two-canvas system — cinematic night for marketing, cream for transactional — with weight-330 display type and pill-only buttons.

hero.title: Everything you need to sell anywhere
hero.sub: One back office for your online store, your market stall, your Instagram and your wholesale orders. Set up in an afternoon, and keep the inventory in one place.

features.title: One back office, every channel
features.sub: Inventory, orders and customers in one place, wherever the sale actually happened.

items.title: Online store
items.body: A themed storefront you can edit without code, on a CDN, with checkout that converts.

items.title: Point of sale
items.body: The same inventory on a card reader at a market stall or a permanent shop floor.

items.title: Social selling
items.body: Product tags on social posts that check out in the app, syncing stock back automatically.

items.title: Inventory
items.body: One stock count across every channel and location, reserved at checkout rather than at fulfilment.

items.title: Shipping
items.body: Discounted labels, tracked from the admin, with returns your customer can start themselves.

items.title: Analytics
items.body: Which channel, which product, which margin — including the shipping and fee costs most reports quietly omit.

showcases.title: The checkout is the product
showcases.body: Accelerated wallets, address autofill from a network of returning shoppers, and a one-page flow that removes the steps where carts get abandoned. Merchants moving from a generic cart typically see a mid-single-digit conversion lift.
points: Fraud scoring in the same round trip

showcases.title: The market stall and the website agree
showcases.body: Point of sale runs on the same inventory as the online store, so a sale at a Saturday market decrements the stock a customer sees online that afternoon. No reconciliation, no spreadsheet on Monday.

gallery.title: Merchants
gallery.sub: A few of the businesses running on Marketside this year.

testimonial.quote: We sold at a market on Saturday and the website stock was right on Sunday morning without anyone touching a spreadsheet. That is the entire reason we moved.
testimonial.name: Aoife Brennan

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Three days free, then one month for a pound. Card rates published per plan.

tiers.name: BASIC
tiers.desc: For a new business selling online.

tiers.name: GROW
tiers.desc: For a growing business with a shop floor.

items.a: Published per plan and per region — 2.9% plus 30¢ online on Basic, dropping to 2.4% on Advanced. In-person rates are lower and listed on the same page.

items.q: Can I use my own domain?
items.a: Yes, on every plan. Buy it through us or connect one you already own; the certificate is issued and renewed automatically either way.

items.q: What happens to my data if I leave?
items.a: Products, customers and orders export as CSV at any time. Theme files are yours to download. There is no export fee and no notice period.
No, for a standard store — themes are edited visually. A developer helps for bespoke checkout logic or a custom storefront, and there is a full API for both.

cta.title: Start selling today
cta.sub: Three days free, then one month for a pound. No card to start the trial.

footer.tagline: One back office for every way you sell.

notes: Two canvases that never blend: cinematic night for marketing storytelling, cream and light for transactional surfaces.
The pill is the only button shape across both tracks. Rounded rectangles do not exist for buttons in this system.
Thin-weight (330) display type is the signature — 96px at weight 330 is the brand's loudest visual, and bolding it destroys the effect.
Aloe and pistachio greens belong to the light track only, where they signal commerce and transactional success.
Photography is full-bleed and edge-to-edge on the cinematic track, never inset into cards. Merchants do the visual lifting that gradients would do elsewhere.
